summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived list of NBA annual scoring leaders. It records single-season scoring records held by Wilt Chamberlain and Kevin Durant, the youngest scoring leader, and the most recent leaders named in the text. It also counts career scoring titles, with Michael Jordan leading at ten, and notes the players who won both the scoring title and the championship in the same season.
one_line: Wikipedia list of NBA annual scoring leaders, covering season scoring records, scoring-title counts, and players who won the scoring title and the championship in the same season.
key_facts: Wilt Chamberlain holds the all-time records for total points scored in a season (4,029) and points per game in a season (50.4), both achieved in the 1961-62 season.
Wilt Chamberlain holds the rookie record for points per game, averaging 37.6 points in the 1959-60 season.
Among active players, Kevin Durant has the highest season point total (2,593) and the highest season scoring average (32.0), both achieved in the 2013-14 season.
Kevin Durant, at 21 years and 197 days, is the youngest scoring leader in NBA history, averaging 30.1 points in the 2009-10 season.
Russell Westbrook averaged a career-high 31.6 points in the 2016-17 season and led the league in scoring that season.
Russell Westbrook became the second NBA player to average a triple-double in a season during the 2016-17 season.
Michael Jordan has won the most scoring titles, with ten.
Jordan and Wilt Chamberlain are the only players to have won seven consecutive scoring titles; this was also Chamberlain's career total.
George Gervin, Allen Iverson and Kevin Durant have each won four scoring titles in their careers.
George Mikan, Neil Johnston and Bob McAdoo have each won three scoring titles.
Paul Arizin, Bob Pettit, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Shaquille O'Neal, Tracy McGrady, Kobe Bryant and Russell Westbrook have each won the scoring title twice.
Since the 1946-47 season, five players have won both the scoring title and the NBA championship in the same season.

Those five players are Fulks in 1947 with the Philadelphia Warriors, Mikan from 1949 to 1950 with the Minneapolis Lakers, Abdul-Jabbar (then Lew Alcindor) in 1971 with the Milwaukee Bucks, Jordan from 1991 to 1993 and from 1996 to 1998 with the Chicago Bulls, and O'Neal in 2000 with the Los Angeles Lakers.
Since the introduction of the three-point field goal, Shaquille O'Neal is the only scoring leader to have made no three-pointers in his winning season.
